Class GTNetInstanceIdentity

java.lang.Object
grafiosch.gtnet.GTNetInstanceIdentity
@Component public class GTNetInstanceIdentity extends Object
Proves that a URL leads back to this running instance, so that GTNet can tell its own entry from the entry of a peer.

The address of an entry cannot answer that question. Behind IPv4 NAT, inside a container or behind a reverse proxy, the public name resolves to an address that no network interface of this machine carries, and two instances on one host share every address and differ only in the port. What the URL leads to is instead established by asking it: this instance draws a random challenge, sends it to the URL and accepts the URL as its own only if the answer is the HMAC of that challenge under a key that never leaves this process. A peer that has never seen the key cannot produce the answer.

The key is drawn anew at every start and is not stored. A challenge is answered only by the process that is running when it is asked, which is exactly the question, and nothing persistent can leak. A server that merely relays the request to this instance passes the check, because it is then indistinguishable from a reverse proxy — whoever enters such a URL as the own address has chosen to be reached through it.

      public boolean isWellFormedChallenge(String challenge)
